'''Gautam Kamath''' is a computer scientist known for his work in [[robust statistics|algorithmic robust statistics]] and [[differential privacy]]. He is an assistant professor at the [[David R. Cheriton School of Computer Science]] at the [[University of Waterloo]], a faculty member at the [[Vector Institute (Canada)|Vector Institute]], and a Canada CIFAR AI Chair.<ref name="cifar">{{cite web |title=Gautam Kamath |url=https://cifar.ca/bios/gautam-kamath/ |publisher=[[CIFAR]] |access-date=July 25, 2026}}</ref> He received the 2026 [[Gödel Prize]] and the 2026 [[Presburger Award]].<ref name="godel-citation" /><ref name="nyu" />

== Education and career ==
Kamath received a Bachelor of Science from [[Cornell University]] in 2012, and a Master of Science (2014) and PhD (2018) from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name="waterloo-profile">{{cite web |title=Gautam Kamath |url=https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/about/people/gckamath |publisher=Cheriton School of Computer Science, University of Waterloo |access-date=July 25, 2026}}</ref> He was a Microsoft Research Fellow at the [[Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing]] before joining the University of Waterloo as an assistant professor in 2019.<ref name="jubilee">{{cite web |title=Gautam Kamath receives Faculty of Math Golden Jubilee Research Excellence Award |url=https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/news/gautam-kamath-receives-faculty-of-math-golden-jubilee-research-excellence-award |publisher=Cheriton School of Computer Science, University of Waterloo |date=2024 |access-date=July 25, 2026}}</ref> He is expected to join the Computer Science department at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at [[New York University]] in September 2026.<ref name="nyu">{{cite web |title=Gautam Kamath Awarded 2026 Gödel Prize |url=https://cims.nyu.edu/dynamic/news/1512/ |publisher=Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences, New York University |access-date=July 25, 2026}}</ref>

== Research ==
Kamath's research concerns algorithms and machine learning under constraints such as data privacy and robustness.<ref name="cifar" />

With Ilias Diakonikolas, [[Daniel Kane (mathematician)|Daniel Kane]], Jerry Li, [[Ankur Moitra]], and Alistair Stewart, Kamath co-authored the paper "Robust Estimators in High-Dimensions without the Computational Intractability", first presented at the 2016 [[Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science]] and published in the ''[[SIAM Journal on Computing]]'' in 2019.<ref name="godel-citation">{{cite web |title=The 2026 Gödel Prize |url=https://www.sigact.org/prizes/g%C3%B6del/citation2026.html |publisher=[[ACM SIGACT]] |access-date=July 25, 2026}}</ref> The paper gave the first polynomial-time algorithms for high-dimensional estimation in the presence of adversarially corrupted data with error guarantees independent of the dimension, resolving a longstanding problem in robust statistics.<ref name="godel-citation" /> The work is credited with establishing the area of algorithmic high-dimensional robust statistics.<ref name="ucsd">{{cite web |title=UC San Diego Professor Daniel Kane Awarded Gödel Prize, Highest Theoretical Computer Science Honor |url=https://today.ucsd.edu/story/uc-san-diego-professor-daniel-kane-awarded-goedel-prize-highest-theoretical-computer-science-honor |publisher=[[University of California, San Diego]] |date=June 2026 |access-date=July 25, 2026}}</ref>

With Clément Canonne and Thomas Steinke, Kamath developed the discrete Gaussian mechanism for differential privacy, presented at [[NeurIPS]] 2020, which was deployed in the [[2020 United States census]].<ref name="pet">{{cite web |title=Gautam Kamath and colleagues win 2024 Caspar Bowden PET Award |url=https://uwaterloo.ca/computer-science/news/gautam-kamath-and-colleagues-win-2024-caspar-bowden-pet |publisher=Cheriton School of Computer Science, University of Waterloo |date=2024 |access-date=July 25, 2026}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
* [[Gödel Prize]], 2026, with Ilias Diakonikolas, Daniel Kane, Jerry Li, Ankur Moitra, and Alistair Stewart, for "Robust Estimators in High-Dimensions without the Computational Intractability"<ref name="godel-citation" />
* [[Presburger Award]] of the [[European Association for Theoretical Computer Science]], 2026<ref name="nyu" />
* Caspar Bowden Award for Outstanding Research in Privacy Enhancing Technologies, 2024, with Clément Canonne and Thomas Steinke, for "The Discrete Gaussian for Differential Privacy"<ref name="pet" />
* Best paper award, [[International Conference on Machine Learning]] (ICML), 2024, with Florian Tramèr and Nicholas Carlini<ref name="icml">{{cite web |title=Gautam Kamath and international colleagues win best paper award at ICML 2024 |url=https://uwaterloo.ca/computer-science/news/gautam-kamath-and-international-colleagues-win-best-paper-at-icml-2024 |publisher=Cheriton School of Computer Science, University of Waterloo |date=2024 |access-date=July 25, 2026}}</ref>
* Canada CIFAR AI Chair<ref name="cifar" />
